patches.replacement_claim: The stem asks whether community and/or political party representatives approached the interviewer, so the item records contact of the field team rather than the respondent's partisanship or perceived influence.
patches.exact_source_quote: Were you approached by community and/or political party representatives?
patches.reason: Quote is literal from Q106C question_text and the reworded claim stays within it.

patches.replacement_claim: The item records a physically threatened experience during the interview encounter, so it does not record threats reported by the respondent or events in the enumeration area.
patches.exact_source_quote: Were you physically threatened during the interview?
patches.reason: Quote is literal from Q106E question_text, anchoring the interview-encounter reading.

patches.replacement_claim: The interviewer rates the respondent's attitude during the interview on a three-way scale, so the item records demeanour in one encounter rather than a validated measure of truthful answers.
patches.reason: Quote is literal from Q109F response_options_all and supports the three-way demeanour claim.

patches.replacement_claim: The forced choice offers presidential exemption from law and courts against obligatory obedience, so it records an abstract constitutional stance and not a verdict on any named court ruling or president.
patches.exact_source_quote: must always obey the laws and the courts
patches.reason: Quote is literal from Q28 question_text and carries the obedience-versus-exemption framing.
The cited phrase appears in the negative statement text but the cross-item comparison to a separate 'army should come in to govern' item has no literal support in the packet.

patches.replacement_claim: The question asks who should be responsible for oversight, so it records a normative allocation of accountability rather than a report that any overseer actually acted.
patches.reason: Quote is literal from Q48A question_text, supporting the normative-allocation reading.
The cited phrase appears in the negative statement text but the byte-identical option-set comparison to Q48A is not asserted in the source metadata.

patches.replacement_claim: The respondent rates the likelihood that a hypothetical woman candidate in the community would be criticized, called names, or harassed, so it records an anticipated social reaction rather than reported experience.
patches.exact_source_quote: she will be criticized, called names, or harassed
patches.reason: Quote is literal from Q50B question_text and supports the anticipated-reaction reading.

patches.replacement_claim: The item asks whether government and elected officials should be doing more or less on women's rights, so a pro-more answer is an evaluative demand rather than evidence that current effort is deficient in fact.
patches.exact_source_quote: should government and elected officials be doing more
patches.reason: Quote is literal from Q51A question_text and carries the demanded-direction framing.
The cited wording appears in the negative statement text, and the option-ordering effect is not stated in the source metadata.

patches.replacement_claim: Agreement is elicited only in the context of a public health emergency about a possible measure, so it endorses a hypothetical emergency policing power rather than describing enforcement that occurred.
patches.exact_source_quote: using the police and security forces to enforce public health mandates
patches.reason: Quote is literal from Q63B question_text and supports the hypothetical-power reading.

patches.replacement_claim: The item records the respondent's belief about who sent the interview team, with the listed responses as distinct sponsorship options, so it is not an audit of the actual commissioning body.
patches.exact_source_quote: Who do you think sent us to do this interview?
patches.reason: Quote is literal from Q97 question_text, anchoring the perceived-sponsorship reading.
The cited phrase appears in the question text but the claim of a separate not-applicable code is only apparent in the special-label list, which the cited quote does not carry.
